corrective_round_1.trigger: tester verdict FAIL on criterion 1 (.legion/test.json criteria.1, head tested 13468c968adb): a worker whose idle-retire clock expired as a no-op while it was phases[issue].phase is never re-armed when phases[issue] later moves to another role; only its own idle transition arms a clock and an already-idle worker never transitions again. Rig: reviewer idle 8.7 min, not the active phase for 5.7 min, no clock pending.
corrective_round_1.spec: Dispatch primary document of LEGION-30 version 6 records the fix in Design and in the New-since-we-talked timer bullet.
corrective_round_1.fix: retireIdleWorker: the predicate order is now disposed -> client identity/idle -> claim/locator/confirmation -> architect -> tree closing/closed -> (pendingAssignment !== undefined || phases[issue] names this role and is not completed). A decline on exactly that last disjunction calls armIdleRetire(token, client) inside the same mutateClaim callback (no await between the top-of-callback identity/idle/disposed checks and the re-arm, so they still hold and it cannot interleave with a prompt) and returns; every other decline returns without re-arming. The tree-gone check moved ahead of the re-arm decision so a closing/closed tree never re-arms (closeTree owns that stop). Both doc comments (armIdleRetire: two arm sites; retireIdleWorker: the re-arm paragraph naming the two conditions and why no other decline re-arms) updated in the file's style.

new: re-arms the clock when expiry declines because the role is the active phase, and retires within one further window once phases[issue] moves to another role (the tester's reproduction, role reviewer: fire -> untouched + exactly one new 600_000 wait; phases[root] = planner; fire -> one shutdown, no kill-pane, resumeSessionFile set, launchFailures/promptFailures undefined, zero publications, zero clocks left pending)
re-arms the clock when expiry declines because a pendingAssignment is queued, and retires within one further window once it is cleared

commit.identity_anomaly: 95f0f339's committer is legion-reviewer[bot] (author legion-implementer[bot], Omp-Session trailer correct). Cause, with evidence: the jj user identity every Legion worker commits with is a REPO-scoped config (~/.config/jj/repos/834789e1326b209850cb/config.toml) on the one shared main repo that every issue workspace is a `jj workspace` of (the op log interleaves LEGION-13/-16/-21/-27/-28/-30 operations; the file's mtime 21:11:56 is a rewrite by another tree's provisioning, not this session's). Whichever role was most recently provisioned anywhere flips the identity for every concurrent commit in every workspace; at 21:07:37 it held reviewer. The handoff commit created by that `jj commit` inherited a reviewer AUTHOR and was corrected before push with `jj metaedit --author 'legion-implementer[bot] <271566630+legion-implementer[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>'` (the exact identity the daemon supplies for this phase; jj `--config user.*` pinned for the command). 95f0f339 was left as pushed: its author and trailer are right, CI is green at it, and a describe-rewrite would move the head under the tester/reviewer for a committer field nothing keys off. Escalated to the architect as a daemon defect (per-role identity must be per-process -- JJ_USER/JJ_EMAIL or a per-workspace config -- not written into the shared repo config); not this PR's scope.
